why: I checked both must_not items against the verifier brief. Item 1: Check 3 lists every exported function by name and fails on any `MISSING`. Its PASS line says it "should include add, subtract, multiply and clamp", and the advisory notes that "subtract was undocumented before this change". A README that covers clamp but not subtract cannot pass. Item 2: Check 1 compares exact return values, which only tests clamp's clamping behaviour. Check 2 only needs `instanceof RangeError` and does not require any message. Check 3 needs a mention plus a description of each function, with no required layout. The heading style, RangeError mention and tests are all labelled "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)". Check 4 only needs a zero exit status. One problem outside this criterion: Check 3's regex escapes probably break inside double quotes in the shell, so the command may error. That would make the check unreliable but not stricter than line 3.
